text: The 25.5-hectare loss of tree cover on this property in 2015 was primarily due to forest clearing. The Hansen Global Forest Change data (GFC-2025-v1.13) confirms this event as a significant loss of tree cover (>=30% canopy) in that year. The property had 23 hectares of tree cover in 2000, which was almost entirely lost by 2020, as corroborated by the JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 dataset showing no forest cover remaining. The 2015 event was the largest single loss before the baseline, suggesting large-scale clearing rather than gradual degradation. No further details on the cause (e.g., agriculture, logging, or development) are available in the Earth-observation data.
